evals.name: bare-except-api-and-shell
evals.prompt: Review python-review-workspace/fixtures/bare-except/classify_notes.py before I run it against my notes library. I want to know if the API error handling and subprocess usage are safe.
evals.expected_output: Review catching: bare except in call_api(), shell=True in run_applescript(), os.path.join instead of pathlib, non-atomic write to proposals file, missing type annotations on public functions, no dry-run guard on classify_all(). Verdict SIGNIFICANT ISSUES.

evals.name: missing-dryrun-destructive-script
evals.prompt: Can you review python-review-workspace/fixtures/missing-dryrun/apply_proposals.py? This is the script that will actually delete and move notes, so I want to be sure it's safe.
evals.expected_output: Review catching: no --dry-run flag despite delete_note() and move_note() calls, apply_classifications and apply_dedup have no dry_run parameter, missing load_settings validation. Verdict SIGNIFICANT ISSUES because dry-run guard is absent on destructive operations.

evals.name: good-script-clean-review
evals.prompt: Please review python-review-workspace/fixtures/good-script/export_notes.py — this is a read-only export script I just wrote. Does it follow the project conventions?
evals.expected_output: Review finding no significant issues: load_settings validates required keys, subprocess uses check=True and shell=False, atomic write pattern used, type annotations present. Should note this is read-only so no dry-run guard needed. Verdict LOOKS GOOD.
